subject.title: [Bug]: toolsAllow cannot re-expose core tools in embedded cron runs

question: Should finite isolated cron `toolsAllow` requests for Codex native-owned shell/file names be materialized as exact OpenClaw dynamic tools, or should those runs fail pre-dispatch when exact exposure cannot be guaranteed?
rationale: The upstream Codex app-server does not expose a granular per-turn native shell/file allowlist, and OpenClaw's current code intentionally fails closed for narrow native allowlists, so the permanent behavior is a security-boundary choice rather than a mechanical cleanup.

options.title: Fail closed unless exact exposure is proven
options.body: Return a deterministic non-ok preflight result such as `TOOL_SURFACE_UNAVAILABLE` whenever a finite allowlist requests shell/file tools that cannot be exactly materialized under current gates.

options.title: Materialize exact OpenClaw dynamic tools
options.body: Re-add only the requested OpenClaw dynamic `exec/read/write/edit` equivalents when deny, sandbox, provider, and Codex exclusion policy all allow them, with focused regression coverage.

options.title: Declare finite Codex native allowlists unsupported
options.body: Document that only wildcard or omitted allowlists can use Codex native shell/file tools, but still fix false-green cron status for unavailable required tools.

recommendation.title: Fail closed unless exact exposure is proven
recommendation.body: Return a deterministic non-ok preflight result such as `TOOL_SURFACE_UNAVAILABLE` whenever a finite allowlist requests shell/file tools that cannot be exactly materialized under current gates.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is centered on the Codex native tool boundary, and steipete has the strongest merged history on that surface among the sampled owners.
